# MĀKI Autonomous Systems

MĀKI is a New Zealand company that designs, develops and operates autonomous marine systems, environmental monitoring technology, and unmanned vehicles for scientific, council and industry clients.

## What MĀKI does

- **Autonomous boats (USVs)** — Unmanned Surface Vehicles for bathymetric mapping, water quality monitoring, and water sampling in lakes, rivers, ponds and coastal environments
- **ROVs** — Remotely Operated Vehicles for underwater inspection of submerged structures, dams, pipes and infrastructure
- **Drones / UAVs** — Aerial photogrammetry and topographic mapping
- **IoT monitoring systems** — Custom environmental sensor platforms, AI cameras, and remote monitoring buoys
- **Bathymetric mapping** — High-resolution underwater depth surveys using sonar and RTK GPS
- **Topo-bathymetric surveys** — Combined above-water and underwater mapping in a single dataset
- **Stormwater & treatment pond surveys** — Sediment volume analysis for councils and infrastructure managers
- **Water quality monitoring** — Autonomous real-time data collection for chlorophyll-a, phycocyanin, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, pH and temperature
- **Water reservoir inspection** — Underwater ROV and surface rover inspection of reservoir walls, floors and inlet/outlet structures without dewatering or confined space entry

## Who MĀKI works with

Regional councils, environmental scientists, infrastructure managers, engineering firms, and researchers across New Zealand — including Waikato Regional Council, Ōtorohanga District Council, Western Bay of Plenty District Council, and Buller District Council.

## Key facts

- Based in New Zealand
- Fully in-house hardware, electronics, firmware, software and AI development
- Systems operate up to 2.5 km from controller or indefinitely via cellular connectivity
- IP67-rated equipment, biosecurity-compliant decontamination protocols
- RTK-enabled centimetre-level GPS accuracy

## Case studies

### Lakes Mapping for Waikato Regional Council
MĀKI deployed autonomous USVs to map 12 lakes across the Waikato region for Waikato Regional Council. The project delivered high-resolution bathymetric data, sediment mapping and water quality profiles used to inform freshwater management decisions.
URL: https://www.maki.nz/case-studies/lakes-mapping/

### Topo-Bathymetric Mapping at Aotea Harbour
MĀKI conducted an integrated topo-bathymetric survey of Aotea Harbour for Ōtorohanga District Council — combining USV sonar with drone photogrammetry to produce a seamless 3D dataset of the harbour floor and surrounding land.
URL: https://www.maki.nz/case-studies/aotea-harbour/

### Autonomous Algae Bloom Monitoring
MĀKI deployed a USV during a cyanobacteria bloom event to autonomously collect real-time water quality data across an affected lake — providing Waikato Regional Council with spatial maps of chlorophyll-a and phycocyanin concentrations to guide public safety decisions.
URL: https://www.maki.nz/case-studies/algae-bloom/

### Ngaroto Lake Bathymetric Survey
MĀKI carried out a full bathymetric survey of Ngaroto Lake, producing a high-resolution depth map and sediment volume estimates to support ecological restoration planning.
URL: https://www.maki.nz/case-studies/ngaroto/

### Water Reservoir Inspection with ROV
MĀKI deployed an underwater ROV and surface rover to inspect a drinking water reservoir — capturing HD video of submerged walls, floors and inlet/outlet structures without dewatering or confined space entry. The survey enabled asset condition assessment with zero operational disruption.
URL: https://www.maki.nz/case-studies/rov-reservoir/

### Sediment Analysis for Stormwater & Wastewater Ponds
MĀKI used autonomous USVs to survey stormwater retention ponds and wastewater treatment ponds, generating bathymetric maps and sediment volume calculations to help infrastructure managers plan desludging programmes and meet consent obligations.
URL: https://www.maki.nz/case-studies/sediment-analysis/
